'''Amit Prakash Sharma''' (born April 12, 1968) is an Indian [[Parasitology|parasitologist]] and former director of [[National Institute of Malaria Research]], New Delhi. He is known for his studies on the disease of [[malaria]] and is an elected fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]], [[Indian National Science Academy]], [[The World Academy of Sciences]] and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]]. He has been awarded the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award in Biological Sciences, JC Bose Fellowship, Ranbaxy Science Research Award, Infosys Science Award in Biological Sciences, Om Prakash Bhasin Award in Biological Sciences and Lakshmipat Singhania- IIM Lucknow National Leadership Award.

== Biography ==
Amit Sharma was born on April 12, 1968, in India. He grew up in New Delhi and attended [[Delhi Public School, Mathura Road]]. Later, he went to U.S. for his undergraduate studies to [[Purdue University]], did his master's and PhD at [[Northwestern University]]. He received a PhD in protein crystallography in 1995. He was an Elected Research Fellow at [[St. John's College, Oxford]], and taught at St John's and Trinity Colleges (1996–2000). On his return to India in 2001, he joined as a Group Leader of the Structural Parasitology group in the Molecular Medicine division of the [[International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology]], New Delhi, and a J. C. Bose National Fellow<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellow detail: Dr Amit Prakash Sharma. Indian National Science Academy. |url=https://insaindia.res.in/old_website/detail.php?id=R16-004}}</ref>. From 2019 to 2022 he was Director of the ICMR–[[National Institute of Malaria Research]], New Delhi. In 2022 he was appointed Distinguished Visiting Professor at the [[IIT Bombay|Indian Institute of Technology Bombay]]. He has served on the Council of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] and on the research advisory committees of the [[Bose Institute]], Kolkata, [[Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Thiruvananthapuram|IISER Thiruvananthapuram]] and the [[Indian Council of Medical Research]]. In 2026 he was appointed to the Advisory Board of the Real Time Governance Society, Government of Andhra Pradesh.

== Legacy ==
[[File:Life Cycle of the Malaria Parasite.jpg|thumb|235px|Life cycle of the malaria parasite]]
Sharma's research is focused in the field of [[structural parasitology]], and he has carried out advanced research in [[malaria]] parasite biology<ref name="Awardee  Details: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=352 |title=Awardee Details: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |date=2017-12-28 |website=ssbprize.gov.in |access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref>. He led the ICGEB group of scientists who collaborated with the researchers from the [[Broad Institute]] who discovered a new compound, [[Bicyclic molecule|bicyclic]] [[azetidine]], which showed potential against the [[Plasmodium]] parasite that caused malaria<ref name="New single-dose treatment shows promise in anti-malaria battle">{{Cite news |url=https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/health/policy-and-issues/New-single-dose-treatment-shows-promise-in-anti-malaria-battle/article14634909.ece |title=New single-dose treatment shows promise in anti-malaria battle |last=Prasad |first=R. |date=2016-09-13 |work=The Hindu |access-date=2017-12-28 |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>. 

Sharma's early structural work included the crystal structure of the ''Plasmodium falciparum'' gametocyte protein Pfg27<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sharma |first1=Amit |last2=Sharma |first2=Indu |last3=Kogkasuriyachai |first3=Darin |last4=Kumar |first4=Nirbhay |title=Structure of a gametocyte protein essential for sexual development in Plasmodium falciparum |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nsb899 |journal=Nature Structural & Molecular Biology |date=2003 |language=en |volume=10 |issue=3 |pages=197–203 |doi=10.1038/nsb899 |pmid=12577051 |issn=1545-9993|url-access=subscription }}</ref>  and the structural basis for recognition of the Duffy antigen by the ''Plasmodium vivax'' Duffy-binding-like domain, which is relevant to ''P. vivax'' vaccine development <ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Singh |first1=Saurabh Kumar |last2=Hora |first2=Rachna |last3=Belrhali |first3=Hassan |last4=Chitnis |first4=Chetan E. |last5=Sharma |first5=Amit |title=Structural basis for Duffy recognition by the malaria parasite Duffy-binding-like domain |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nature04443 |journal=Nature |date=2006 |language=en |volume=439 |issue=7077 |pages=741–744 |doi=10.1038/nature04443 |pmid=16372020 |bibcode=2006Natur.439..741S |issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription }}</ref>.

From 2011 his group studied parasite aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases as drug targets, starting with tyrosyl-tRNA synthetase<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bhatt |first1=Tarun Kumar |last2=Khan |first2=Sameena |last3=Dwivedi |first3=Ved Prakash |last4=Banday |first4=Mudassir Meraj |last5=Sharma |first5=Arvind |last6=Chandele |first6=Anmol |last7=Camacho |first7=Noelia |last8=de Pouplana |first8=Lluís Ribas |last9=Wu |first9=Yang |last10=Craig |first10=Alister G. |last11=Mikkonen |first11=Antti Tapani |last12=Maier |first12=Alexander Gerd |last13=Yogavel |first13=Manickam |last14=Sharma |first14=Amit |date=2011-11-08 |title=Malaria parasite tyrosyl-tRNA synthetase secretion triggers pro-inflammatory responses |journal=Nature Communications |language=en |volume=2 |issue=1 |article-number=530 |doi=10.1038/ncomms1522 |doi-access=free |pmid=22068597 |bibcode=2011NatCo...2..530B |issn=2041-1723}}</ref>, and later reported structures of prolyl-, lysyl- and phenylalanyl-tRNA synthetases bound to inhibitors, including bicyclic azetidines <ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sharma |first1=Manmohan |last2=Malhotra |first2=Nipun |last3=Yogavel |first3=Manickam |last4=Harlos |first4=Karl |last5=Melillo |first5=Bruno |last6=Comer |first6=Eamon |last7=Gonse |first7=Arthur |last8=Parvez |first8=Suhel |last9=Mitasev |first9=Branko |last10=Fang |first10=Francis G. |last11=Schreiber |first11=Stuart L. |last12=Sharma |first12=Amit |date=2021-01-12 |title=Structural basis of malaria parasite phenylalanine tRNA-synthetase inhibition by bicyclic azetidines |journal=Nature Communications |language=en |volume=12 |issue=1 |article-number=343 |doi=10.1038/s41467-020-20478-5 |doi-access=free |issn=2041-1723 |pmc=7803973 |pmid=33436639 |bibcode=2021NatCo..12..343S }}</ref>. In 2017 he proposed "structure-based targeting of orthologous pathogen proteins" for drug discovery against several parasites<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jain |first1=Vitul |last2=Yogavel |first2=Manickam |last3=Kikuchi |first3=Haruhisa |last4=Oshima |first4=Yoshiteru |last5=Hariguchi |first5=Norimitsu |last6=Matsumoto |first6=Makoto |last7=Goel |first7=Preeti |last8=Touquet |first8=Bastien |last9=Jumani |first9=Rajiv S. |last10=Tacchini-Cottier |first10=Fabienne |last11=Harlos |first11=Karl |last12=Huston |first12=Christopher D. |last13=Hakimi |first13=Mohamed-Ali |last14=Sharma |first14=Amit |title=Targeting Prolyl-tRNA Synthetase to Accelerate Drug Discovery against Malaria, Leishmaniasis, Toxoplasmosis, Cryptosporidiosis, and Coccidiosis |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0969212617302496 |journal=Structure |date=2017 |language=en |volume=25 |issue=10 |pages=1495–1505.e6 |doi=10.1016/j.str.2017.07.015 |pmid=28867614 }}</ref>, and in 2022 his group showed that two different inhibitors can bind prolyl-tRNA synthetase at the same time<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Manickam |first1=Yogavel |last2=Malhotra |first2=Nipun |last3=Mishra |first3=Siddhartha |last4=Babbar |first4=Palak |last5=Dusane |first5=Abhishek |last6=Laleu |first6=Benoît |last7=Bellini |first7=Valeria |last8=Hakimi |first8=Mohamed-Ali |last9=Bougdour |first9=Alexandre |last10=Sharma |first10=Amit |date=2022-03-25 |editor-last=Clayton |editor-first=Christine |title=Double drugging of prolyl-tRNA synthetase provides a new paradigm for anti-infective drug development |journal=PLOS Pathogens |language=en |volume=18 |issue=3 |article-number=e1010363 |doi=10.1371/journal.ppat.1010363 |doi-access=free |issn=1553-7374 |pmc=9004777 |pmid=35333915}}</ref>.

During the COVID-19 pandemic he co-authored a report of multidrug-resistant ''Candida auris'' infections in critically ill COVID-19 patients in India<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chowdhary |first1=Anuradha |last2=Tarai |first2=Bansidhar |last3=Singh |first3=Ashutosh |last4=Sharma |first4=Amit |title=Multidrug-Resistant Candida auris Infections in Critically Ill Coronavirus Disease Patients, India, April–July 2020 |url=http://wwwnc.cdc.gov/eid/article/26/11/20-3504_article.htm |journal=Emerging Infectious Diseases |date=2020 |volume=26 |issue=11 |pages=2694–2696 |doi=10.3201/eid2611.203504 |issn=1080-6040 |pmc=7588547 |pmid=32852265}}</ref> , and structural work on an antibody that neutralises SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kumar |first1=Sanjeev |last2=Patel |first2=Anamika |last3=Lai |first3=Lilin |last4=Chakravarthy |first4=Chennareddy |last5=Valanparambil |first5=Rajesh |last6=Reddy |first6=Elluri Seetharami |last7=Gottimukkala |first7=Kamalvishnu |last8=Davis-Gardner |first8=Meredith E. |last9=Edara |first9=Venkata Viswanadh |last10=Linderman |first10=Susanne |last11=Nayak |first11=Kaustuv |last12=Dixit |first12=Kritika |last13=Sharma |first13=Pragati |last14=Bajpai |first14=Prashant |last15=Singh |first15=Vanshika |date=2022-10-07 |title=Structural insights for neutralization of Omicron variants BA.1, BA.2, BA.4, and BA.5 by a broadly neutralizing SARS-CoV-2 antibody |journal=Science Advances |language=en |volume=8 |issue=40 |article-number=eadd2032 |doi=10.1126/sciadv.add2032 |issn=2375-2548 |pmc=9534492 |pmid=36197988 |bibcode=2022SciA....8D2032K }}</ref>.

As Director of NIMR he led the development of the NIMR Malaria Dashboard, a digital platform for analysing malaria surveillance data in India<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Yadav |first1=Chander Prakash |last2=Sharma |first2=Amit |title=National Institute of Malaria Research-Malaria Dashboard (NIMR-MDB): A digital platform for analysis and visualization of epidemiological data |journal=The Lancet Regional Health - Southeast Asia |date=2022 |language=en |volume=5 |article-number=100030 |doi=10.1016/j.lansea.2022.100030 |pmc=10305863 |pmid=37383658}}</ref>,and published on malaria elimination strategy, the links between malaria and malnutrition, and climate zones as a factor in malaria epidemiology<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Yadav |first1=Chander Prakash |last2=Hussain |first2=Syed Shah Areeb |last3=Pasi |first3=Shweta |last4=Sharma |first4=Shweta |last5=Bharti |first5=Praveen K |last6=Rahi |first6=Manju |last7=Sharma |first7=Amit |title=Linkages between malaria and malnutrition in co-endemic regions of India |journal=BMJ Global Health |date=2023 |language=en |volume=8 |issue=1 |article-number=e010781 |doi=10.1136/bmjgh-2022-010781 |issn=2059-7908 |pmc=9853155 |pmid=36653068}}</ref>.

His studies have been documented by way of a number of articles<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.labome.org/expert/india/international/sharma/amit-sharma-501912.html |title=Amit Sharma on Labome |last=labome.org |date=2017-12-28 |language=en |access-date=2017-12-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171228232529/https://www.labome.org/expert/india/international/sharma/amit-sharma-501912.html |archive-date=2017-12-28 |url-status=dead }}</ref>. Sharma has published more than 250 research papers and book chapters. His papers have appeared in journals including ''Nature'', ''Science Translational Medicine'', ''Nature Communications'', ''Science Advances'', ''Structure'', ''PLOS Pathogens'' and ''The Lancet Regional Health – Southeast Asia''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Google scholar profile |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=D_40uWAAAAAJ&view_op=list_works}}</ref>''PublicationsList'', an online repository of scientific articles, has listed several of them.<ref name="Amit Sharma - Publications List">{{Cite web |url=http://publicationslist.org/amit.sharma |title=Amit Sharma - Publications List |date=2017-12-28 |website=publicationslist.org |access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref> Sharma has delivered keynote or invited speeches at many conferences<ref name="2005 Malaria Conference GRC">{{Cite web |url=https://www.grc.org/malaria-conference/2005/ |title=2005 Malaria Conference GRC |date=2005 |website=www.grc.org |language=en |access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref><ref name="Programme - CSIR Foundation Day 2012">{{Cite web |url=http://sap.csir.res.in/foundationday2012/Programme.aspx |title=Programme - CSIR Foundation Day 2012 |date=2012 |website=sap.csir.res.in |access-date=2017-12-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171229052135/http://sap.csir.res.in/foundationday2012/Programme.aspx |archive-date=2017-12-29 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and sits on the editorial board of Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, India for Section B - Biological Sciences.<ref name="The National Academy of Sciences, India - Editorial">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/edtboard-b.htm |title=The National Academy of Sciences, India - Editorial |date=2017-12-28 |website=www.nasi.org.in |access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Sharma is an elected fellow of four of India's national science academies and of The World Academy of Sciences:

* National Academy of Sciences, India (NASI), 2006 
* Indian Academy of Sciences (IASc), 2012 
* The World Academy of Sciences (TWAS), 2015<ref>{{Cite web |title="Sharma Amit – TWAS Fellow, elected 2015." The World Academy of Sciences. |url=https://twas.org/member/sharma-amit}}</ref>
* Indian National Science Academy (INSA), 2016<ref>{{Cite web |title="Fellow detail: Dr Amit Prakash Sharma." Indian National Science Academy. |url=https://insaindia.res.in/old_website/detail.php?id=R16-004}}</ref>
* National Academy of Medical Sciences (NAMS), 2022<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellow 2022." National Academy of Medical Sciences (India). |url=https://nams-india.in/downloads/FELLOW%202022.pdf}}</ref>

He has received various national and international honours:

* 1996–2000 – Elected Research Fellow, St John's College, Oxford
* 2001–2006 – Wellcome Trust International Senior Research Fellowship
* 2006 – B. M. Birla Science Prize in Biological Sciences
* 2006 – Bachawat Memorial Award in Biomedical Sciences
* 2006 – Fellow, National Academy of Sciences, India<ref name="NASI Year Book 2015">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |title=NASI Year Book 2015 |date=2017-12-17 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |access-date=2017-12-17}}</ref>
* 2007 – Prof. Umakant Sinha Memorial Award, Indian Science Congress Association
* 2007 – Dr M. O. T. Iyengar National Science Award for Biomedical Research, ICMR
* 2007/2008 – National Bioscience Award for Career Development, Department of Biotechnology<ref name="Awardees of National Bioscience Awards for Career Development">{{Cite web |url=http://dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/list_of_bioscience_awardees.pdf |title=Awardees of National Bioscience Awards for Career Development |date=2016 |publisher=Department of Biotechnology |access-date=2017-11-20 |archive-date=2018-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180304191331/http://dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/list_of_bioscience_awardees.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>
